clue.text: Bar essentially trendy, bitter's chilled

indicators.note: bar can mean except or without, so something is left out of the word that follows

parts.note: a bitter person is resentful

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only its central letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A drinker reports that the trendy bar is serving its bitter nicely chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar and bitter look like pub talk, but bar means without and bitter is an adjective: RESENTFUL loses EN to leave RESTFUL. The 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled in its slang sense means relaxed and calm, which is what a restful mood or place is.

clue.text: Plain piece of bread after cycling back from deli's devoured

indicators.note: whatever is devoured ends up inside the eater, so one set of letters swallows another
a cycle goes round, so the front letter travels round to the end of the word

parts.note: the hard outer piece of a loaf

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone buys a plain bit of bread at the deli and eats it on the bike ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUST with its C cycled to the back becomes RUSTC, which then swallows the I to give RUSTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic describes something simple and unsophisticated in a countryside way, so plain is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Possibly oil in first pair of SEATs unchanged

indicators.note: a first pair means the opening two letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the opening two letters of the car brand
what is unchanged stays the same

explanation.surface: A mechanic finds the oil in a couple of SEAT cars has not been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT is a Spanish car maker, so the surface is about servicing; 'Possibly oil' is the definition by example, since sesame is one kind of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame oil is a common cooking oil pressed from the seeds, so sesame is one possible example of oil.

clue.text: Victoria's genuine material for writing pretty thick, but not black, lines

parts.note: fair is an old word for pretty

indicators.note: to line something is to sit along its inside, so one piece goes within another
but not means excluding, so a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: thick and dumb both mean stupid
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
what a pen writes with

explanation.surface: Someone describes ink for writing as pretty thick, though the lines it makes are not black.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is the Australian state, not the queen, so the answer is Australian slang. 'Lines' is a verb: the writing material sits inside the shortened word for thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dinkum is Australian slang meaning honest or genuine, and Victoria is an Australian state, so the phrase is used there.

clue.text: Door maybe not opening? One's unlikely to get in first

definitions.text: One's unlikely to get in first

indicators.note: without its opening, a word has lost its first letter

parts.note: a door is one example of a thing that closes

explanation.surface: A door won't open, and whoever is stuck behind it will hardly be first through.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a door is only maybe a closer. Removing the C leaves LOSER; 'get in first' means finish first in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who habitually fails to win, so they are rarely first past the post.

clue.text: Cycle was hard with pressure on to take the lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front, so these letters are placed at the start

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means on, as in 'on the subject of'
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cyclist found the ride hard work and pressed on to get ahead of the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycle is a washing-machine programme, not a bike. RE meaning 'on' (as in a letter's subject line) is a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wash is one of the programmes on a washing machine, run before the main wash.

clue.text: Mentions tips on solving cryptically?

indicators.note: the setter asks for a crossword reading of the answer itself, where its second word is a signal to rearrange

parts.note: the letters that come out of the rearrangement
in crosswords, out often tells you to rearrange the word next to it

explanation.surface: Someone offers advice on how to solve cryptic crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: read the answer as a clue, POINTS + OUT, and the rearranged POINTS gives 'tips on', the phrase in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To point something out is to draw attention to it, which is what mentioning it does.

clue.text: Hunk cutting wife's fringe

indicators.note: cutting something removes it, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a hunk of cheese or cake is a wedge
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A handsome hunk is trimming his wife's fringe.
explanation.walkthrough: Hunk looks like a handsome man, but it is a chunk of something. 'Wife’s fringe' reads as one phrase; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is the outer margin or border of something, which is its edge.

clue.text: Learned cooler half of Bordeaux's inspired by Zola's final chapter

indicators.note: to be inspired is to be breathed in, so one piece is drawn inside another

parts.note: AC, air conditioning, cools a room

indicators.note: final means last, so only the end letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the French novelist's name
demi is French for half, and Bordeaux is in France
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A scholar notes that Zola's final chapter drew on a cool Bordeaux wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Half a bottle of Bordeaux suggests drinking; really Bordeaux just signals French, and the French word for half is wanted. AC for air conditioning is a common crossword cooler.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic describes scholarly, bookish learning, so a learned person or work is academic.

clue.text: Weapons buried in outbreaks of peace?

definitions.text: Weapons buried in outbreaks of peace?

parts.note: surface reading: arms hidden underground when fighting stops
setter's reading: the idiom for making peace is to bury a particular small axe

explanation.walkthrough: To 'bury the hatchet' is an idiom for making peace, so whenever peace breaks out, these weapons are figuratively buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatchets are small axes that can serve as arms, and the idiom about ending a quarrel is about burying one.

clue.text: One's upset about American hospital food

indicators.note: something upset is tipped over, so the letters run the other way
about means around, so these letters wrap round others

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) is I + S
US is short for American
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient complains about the food in an American hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset suggests an unhappy patient, but it turns the first two letters over; one's is read as 'one is', I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so it is a type of food.

clue.text: Man aboard small boat gets emergency medical cover

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a man on a board is a chess piece, here the most important one
a raft is a simple flat boat

explanation.surface: A man in a little boat calls for emergency medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man aboard' sounds like a sailor, but the board is a chessboard and the man is a piece on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft covers a wound or burn with transplanted tissue, a cover applied by surgeons, often after injury.

clue.text: Current price to get hold of male fashion becoming excessive

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so one piece clasps another

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a rate is a price charged
M is the abbreviation for male
the mode is the current fashion

explanation.surface: Men's fashion is getting so pricey that the prices have become excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: I and RATE together hold M and MODE: I-MMODE-RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderate means lacking restraint and going beyond reasonable limits, the same idea as excessive.

clue.text: Accommodating each youth on vacation is okay

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one piece houses another
a word on vacation has emptied out, so only its outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Putting up every young person who is on holiday is fine by the host.
explanation.walkthrough: Y and H are what remain of 'youth' when its middle has gone away; they hold EA.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeah is the informal form of yes, an expression of agreement just like okay.

clue.text: Shows off with job people looked up to

parts.note: a role is a job or function
to model clothes is to show them off

explanation.surface: Someone who boasts about their job, as if everyone admires them.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the two parts in reverse order: the job comes first in the answer, the showing off second.
explanation.definitionFit: Role models are people whose behaviour others admire and copy, so they are looked up to.

clue.text: See, cutting egotism not complicated for fan of six-footers

indicators.note: something cutting into a word goes inside it
complicated means tangled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: Notice how self-regard, if kept simple, appeals to fans of very tall people.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footers sounds like tall people, but insects have six feet. The rearranged EGOTISMNOT is cut by LO.
explanation.definitionFit: An entomologist studies insects, the creatures with six legs, so is a jokey enthusiast of six-footers.

clue.text: After due consideration, loan can be dealt with

indicators.note: cards that are dealt are scattered out, so these letters are shuffled into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank manager decides, after thinking it over, that the loan can be arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is both part of the letters and part of the surface sense; all of 'loan can be' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: On balance means having weighed all the factors, which is what deciding after due consideration involves.

clue.text: Look to pinch empty store's doormat?

indicators.note: pinching grips something between two fingers, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: to look tired is to appear tired

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its middle, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A thief looks to steal the welcome mat from a closed-down shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Look is a verb meaning seem, not see; the question mark warns that doormat is figurative, a person rather than a mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others walk over them, just as an appeaser gives in to keep others happy.

clue.text: Maybe Tiger Woods's ultimate eating demand — raspberries

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so these letters take in the next ones

parts.note: a tiger is one example of a big cat
a call for something is a demand for it

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of the golfer's surname

explanation.surface: The golfer Tiger Woods finally sits down to a dessert of raspberries he insisted on.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiger Woods is not the golfer but a cat plus the S that ends Woods. CATS eats CALL. A raspberry is a rude blowing noise of derision.
explanation.definitionFit: Raspberries are rude spluttering noises of contempt, and catcalls are similarly jeering shouts aimed at performers.

clue.text: Club sandwiches possibly tuna with half of best spread

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its outer layers, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters, not the given one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of a word is just one half of its letters, here the opening pair

parts.note: the first half of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: A club sandwich might contain tuna along with the best spread.
explanation.walkthrough: Club sandwich is a real snack, but club is a golf club, PUTTER, which sandwiches the rearranged TUNA plus BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a paste of ground nuts that is spread on bread, so it is a spread.

clue.text: Dress from Crew, with old red covering

indicators.note: a covering goes round what it covers, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: Che Guevara, the dead Marxist revolutionary, is an old red
a lot is a group of people, a crew

explanation.surface: A dress from the store J.Crew comes with an old red cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is a communist here, not a colour, and old because Guevara died in 1967; Crew is not the clothing brand but a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone is to put clothes on them, which is what clothe means as a verb.

clue.text: Absentee soldier, largely faithful to the crown

indicators.note: largely means mostly, so the word loses its last letter
the crown is the top, and in a down clue these letters sit above the rest

parts.note: faithful and true both mean loyal
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier who has gone missing is mostly still loyal to the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier seems military, but it is an insect: ANT goes below TRU in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is someone absent without permission, especially a pupil skipping school, so an absentee.

clue.text: Referee starts action taking only seconds before Hearts score

indicators.note: taking only the seconds means keeping the second letter of each word

parts.note: the second letter of each of the three words
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A football referee gets play going, and within seconds Hearts score.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club in the surface; here it is the card suit. Score is a verb, not a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to scratch lines into it, which is what etching does with a needle or acid.

clue.text: Beat It belted out by Nick, which may be useful for Queen?

definitions.text: which may be useful for Queen?

indicators.note: belting out a song means singing it loudly, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: beat it is slang for run away
to nick and to collar are both slang for arrest

explanation.surface: Michael Jackson's 'Beat It' is sung loudly by someone called Nick, perhaps handy for the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is not the band or the monarch: a queen is a female cat. Nick is not a name but means arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen is a female cat, and a collar treated against parasites keeps fleas off a pet.

clue.text: Right to stop a relative lighting up?

indicators.note: a stopper fills a gap, so this letter is plugged into the middle

parts.note: a son is one relative
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A family member insists on the right to stop a relative from smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighting up suggests a cigarette, but the question mark points to setting a building on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, so whimsically a kind of lighting up.

clue.text: Prison disturbances on reflection out of the ordinary

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters run back to front
out of means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: riots are violent disturbances
O was the ordinary level in British school exams

explanation.surface: Looking back, the prison riots were unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the ordinary' looks like a single phrase meaning unusual, but it splits into a deletion of O from RIOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old British slang for prison, as in 'doing time in stir'.

clue.text: Breaking locks, criminal slept in with police officer

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so these letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
DS is a Detective Sergeant

explanation.surface: A burglar picks the locks and then sleeps over, along with a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking locks suggests burglary; really the locks are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are hairs whose tips have frayed into two, so locks of hair that are breaking.

clue.text: Remarkably, actor unneeded

definitions.meaning: first meaning: especially or exceptionally, as in very kind
second meaning: a film performer in a crowd scene
third meaning: surplus, more than is required

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, the actor was not required after all.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one short word, joined to look like a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means exceptionally as an adverb, a non-speaking background performer as a noun, and surplus as an adjective.

clue.text: Military force evacuated refuge before first strike?

indicators.note: something evacuated has had its inside cleared, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
in tennis the serve is the first hit of each point

explanation.surface: An army pulls out of its shelter before launching a pre-emptive attack.
explanation.walkthrough: First strike sounds like a military attack; the question mark points to the opening hit in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: The reserve is the part of an army held back from action, so a military force in its own right.

clue.text: Our French bread ingredient not hot, don't worry

parts.note: nos is French for our

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: flour from wheat goes into bread
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A French baker reassures us that our bread is fine even without heat.
explanation.walkthrough: NOS is the French plural form of our; WHEAT without H gives WEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal idiom meaning there's no problem, which is a way of telling someone not to worry.
